+The pattern can also be any constant expression, such as a call to `CONCAT` or `TO_LOWER`.
+from employees | where first_name like concat("Eber", "*") | keep emp_no, first_name
+The pattern can also be any constant expression, such as a call to `CONCAT` or `TO_UPPER`.
+from employees | where first_name rlike concat("Eber", ".*") | keep emp_no, first_name

usually acts on a field placed on the left-hand side of the operator, but it can

represents the pattern.

* `*` matches zero or more characters.
* `?` matches one character.",

@@ -1536,3 +1536,401 @@ from employees | eval n = first_name | where n like "*" | stats c = count(*);
+// Constant expression on the RHS of LIKE/RLIKE (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/147671)
+from employees | where first_name like concat("Eber", "*") | keep emp_no, first_name
+from employees | where first_name rlike concat("Eber", ".*") | keep emp_no, first_name
+// to_upper folds at optimization time; the resulting pattern matches the uppercase string case-sensitively
+from employees | eval p = "Eber*" | where first_name like p | keep emp_no, first_name;
+from employees | eval p = concat("Eber", "*") | where first_name like p | keep emp_no, first_name;
+from employees | eval p = concat("Eber", ".*") | where first_name rlike p | keep emp_no, first_name;
+row abc = "demo" | eval filter = concat("demo", "*") | where abc like filter | keep abc;
+row abc = "demo" | eval filter = concat("demo", ".*") | where abc rlike filter | keep abc;
+from employees | eval p = "Eber.*" | where first_name rlike p | keep emp_no, first_name;
+from employees | eval suffix = "*" | eval p = concat("Eber", suffix) | where first_name like p | keep emp_no, first_name;
+from employees | eval suffix = ".*" | eval p = concat("Eber", suffix) | where first_name rlike p | keep emp_no, first_name;
+from employees | where first_name not like concat("Eber", "*") | keep emp_no, first_name | sort emp_no | limit 3;
+from employees | where first_name not rlike concat("Eber", ".*") | keep emp_no, first_name | sort emp_no | limit 3;
+// Constant expression on the RHS: broader coverage (prefix/suffix/contains, multi-value fields,
+// upstream commands, escaping, aggregations and joins). See https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/147671
+from employees | where first_name like concat("*", "ki") | keep emp_no, first_name | sort emp_no;
+from employees | where first_name like concat("*", "ann", "*") | keep emp_no, first_name | sort emp_no;
+from employees | where first_name like concat("Georgi", "") | keep emp_no, first_name;
+// job_positions is a multi-value field; expand it first, then match individual values with the constant pattern
+from employees | keep emp_no, job_positions | mv_expand job_positions | where job_positions like concat("Account", "*") | stats c = count(*);
+from employees | keep emp_no, job_positions | mv_expand job_positions | where job_positions like concat("Sen", "*") | stats c = count(*);
+from employees | eval n = first_name | where n like concat("Eb", "*") | keep emp_no, first_name | sort emp_no;
+from employees | grok first_name "%{WORD:g}" | where g like concat("Eb", "*") | keep emp_no | sort emp_no;
+row s = "hello world" | dissect s "%{a} %{b}" | where b like concat("wor", "*") | keep b;
+from employees | where to_lower(first_name) like concat(to_lower("EBER"), "*") | keep emp_no | sort emp_no;
+from employees | where to_upper(first_name) rlike concat(to_upper("eber"), ".*") | keep emp_no | sort emp_no;
+// a match-all pattern folds to IsNotNull, so null gender values are excluded
+from employees | where gender like concat("", "*") | stats c = count(*);
+from employees | where first_name like concat("zzz", "*") | stats c = count(*);
+// the escaped "\*" is a literal star, so it matches the literal "a*b" and not an arbitrary string
+row x = "a*b" | where x like concat("a", "\\*", "b") | keep x;
+row x = "a?b" | where x rlike concat("a\\?", "b") | keep x;
+from employees | stats c = count(*) by gender | where gender like concat("M", "*") | keep gender, c;
+from employees | stats c = count(*) by gender | where to_string(c) like concat("5", "*") | keep gender, c;
+from employees | eval x = to_string(languages) | enrich languages_policy on x | where language_name like concat("Eng", "*") | stats c = count(*);
+from employees | eval language_code = languages | lookup join languages_lookup on language_code | where first_name like concat("Eb", "*") | keep emp_no, first_name, language_name | sort emp_no;
+from employees | eval language_code = languages | lookup join languages_lookup on language_code | where language_name rlike concat("Eng", ".*") | stats c = count(*);
+from employees | inline stats total = count(*) | where first_name like concat("Eb", "*") | keep emp_no, first_name, total | sort emp_no;
+from employees | fork (where first_name like concat("Eb", "*")) (where first_name like concat("Ge", "*")) | stats c = count(*) by _fork | sort _fork;
+// an empty pattern folds to an exact match on the empty string
+row x = "" | where x like concat("", "") | keep x;

+from employees | eval p = concat("Eb", "*"), language_code = languages | lookup join languages_lookup on language_code | where first_name like p | keep emp_no, first_name, language_name | sort emp_no;
+from sample_data | lookup join message_types_lookup on message | where message like concat("Connect", "*") | stats c = count(*);
+from employees | inline stats c = count(*) by starts_eb = first_name like concat("Eb", "*") | keep emp_no, first_name, starts_eb, c | sort emp_no | limit 3;
+        // DeferredRegexExpression is a parse-time placeholder for LIKE/RLIKE with a
+        // non-literal constant-expression pattern (e.g. WHERE field LIKE CONCAT(...)). It is
+        // not a Function and is not in CLASS_NAME_TO_OPERATOR_NAME (only the resolved
+        // WildcardLike/RLike classes are). Without this case the tracking context from the
+        // enclosing Not would leak through and the field at position 0 would be recorded as
+        // "NOT:0 is covered" instead of the correct "LIKE:0" / "RLIKE:0".
| valueExpression (NOT)? LIKE LP stringOrParameter (COMMA stringOrParameter )* RP   #likeListExpression
| valueExpression (NOT)? RLIKE LP stringOrParameter (COMMA stringOrParameter )* RP  #rlikeListExpression

+ * A temporary placeholder for a {@code LIKE} or {@code RLIKE} predicate whose pattern is a
+ * non-literal constant expression (e.g. {@code WHERE field LIKE CONCAT("prefix", "*")}).
+ * Unlike {@link WildcardLike}/{@link RLike}, this node has two children: the field (LHS)
+ * and the pattern expression (RHS). Having both as children ensures the standard analyzer tree
+ * walk resolves the pattern expression through the normal reference/function resolution rules.
+ * After analysis the optimizer's {@code PropagateEvalFoldables} and {@code ConstantFolding} rules
+ * run on the pattern child. A subsequent optimizer rule ({@code ReplaceDeferredRegex}) then
+ * replaces this node with a concrete {@link WildcardLike} or {@link RLike} once the pattern is
+ * foldable to a string. Any node that survives to post-optimization verification is reported as
+public class DeferredRegexExpression extends Expression implements PostOptimizationVerificationAware {
+    /** Which regex operator this placeholder represents. */
+    public DeferredRegexExpression(Source source, Expression field, Expression patternExpression, Variant variant) {
+     * Validates the field (LHS) type at analysis time, mirroring {@link WildcardLike}/{@link RLike}
+     * Using {@code isStringAndExact} would reject text fields without a keyword sub-field, which
+     * would be accepted by the literal-pattern path. The pattern (RHS) type/foldability is not known
+     * until after optimizer folding and is checked in {@link #postOptimizationVerification}.
+     * Validates the pattern after the optimizer has run constant folding and eval propagation.
+     * Any {@code DeferredRegexExpression} that survives to this point means the optimizer's
+     * {@code ReplaceDeferredRegex} rule could not convert it: the pattern has a non-string type,
+     * is not foldable (e.g. a field reference), or the optimizer reduced it to a null literal.
+     * The null check uses {@link Expressions#isGuaranteedNull} rather than folding again: after
+     * {@code ConstantFolding} has run, any expression that evaluated to null is already represented
+     * as a {@code Literal(null)} in the tree, so no new fold is needed here.
+                    "[{}] pattern must be a string, found [{}]",
